newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ad market to grow 3.2 pct in 1997 - Havas.
newsitem.headline: French ad market to grow 3.2 pct in 1997 - Havas.

text.p: The French advertising market should expand by around 3.2 percent in 1997 after growing just under three percent last year, Alain Neuville, research director of Havas Intermediation, said on Wednesday.
In 1995, the market totalled 29 billion francs ($5.2 billion).
"We're expecting a small rise in 1997, an increase of around 3.2 percent," Neuville told Reuters. He said he expected a five percent rise in television advertising but no growth in radio ads.
"For 1996, we'll have done slightly less than the 3.3 percent we forecast in June," he said, adding that it looked like the market had grown just under three percent.
"Last year we had expected an improvement to begin in the summer, and that happened in Europe but not in France," he said.
He said the Paris car show, which took place in October and normally provides an advertising boost, "did not keep its promises".
Television advertising came in below expectations of 5.7 percent growth. "We'll be well under five percent," he said.

"There was no growth in radio advertising. Ads in media publications will exceed provisions of 2.1 percent. Billboards, which rose 2.2 percent in 1995, grew between 2.5 and three percent in 1996," he said.
Advertising in cinemas grew last year at the rapid 7.9 percent pace of 1995, he said.

Last week, consultants Ipsos forecast a 4.9 percent rise in advertising in 1997 to 31.6 billion francs after surveying 150 managers whose combined advertising budgets exceed 2.5 billion francs. Excluding television, Ipsos predicted advertising would rise three percent to 16.5 billion francs.
